T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — EU Critical Raw Materials Act 2030 targets; US $12bn reserve buildout; supply chain diversification strategies

Synopsis:
China's dominance in rare earth mining (~70%) and processing (~90%) is a structural geopolitical and supply chain risk that came back into sharp focus via the US-China trade war. Beijing's export curbs forced a US policy pivot toward domestic reserves and a 54-nation critical minerals coalition. Europe is also responding via the 2025 Critical Raw Materials Act and France's processing capacity, but is widely seen as moving too slowly. Ecological risks from expanding extraction into Brazil, Greenland and South Africa are flagged. Innovation in recycling and waste extraction is promising but insufficient to offset raw extraction demand.

Supply chain constraints on rare earths could indirectly affect the pace and cost of renewable deployment, with downstream implications for German power market fundamentals.
